answers.answer: Roll one die simultaneously for each held office card, adding one for each fatigue on that card and one more for the Chairman. A modified 1–2 has no effect, 3–4 adds fatigue, and 5+ retires the member: move the member to Pensioners, flip the office card into Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to the supply.
answers.evidence: London Season—Attrition: office die plus fatigue; Chairman also adds one; 5+ retire; move retiree to Pensioners, flip card into Vacant Offices, return fatigue to supply.

answers.answer: Only players who retired at least one pensioner may select a London Season display card. They act in descending order of their actual total retirement spending. Ties go first to the player with the most total windows, counting new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. Each eligible player takes or discards one display card; the acting player may peek at display blackmails. Afterward discard all cards still in the display and refill it with exactly three cards (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if nobody selected a card. Return all remaining Pensioners to their supplies.
answers.evidence: London Season—Prestige: players who retired at least one; descending actual retirement spending; ties by total windows then clockwise from PM; discard remaining cards and refill exactly three; return Pensioners to supplies.

answers.answer: A player's opportunity marker starts off the board. If it was already on the chosen action at the start of the Family phase, that action may be taken twice. An extra-action law grants an additional action using only the latest passed extra-action law; that extra action is not doubled by the marker and does not move it. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer places one additional writer once that turn. Since the marker is already on Enlist Writer, the action can be taken twice, so up to three writers can be placed total.
answers.evidence: Family phase: marker already on action at phase start allows it twice; latest extra-action law only, with no marker doubling or movement. Enlist Writer: with at least four vacant offices place one additional writer once this turn, so doubled action can place three total.

answers.answer: After all Family actions, while Debt and applicants both remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court as a Company share and lower Debt by one; repeat while both conditions hold. If Debt is gone, slide the remaining applicants as far right as possible while preserving their order. The initial money for seeking a share was paid to the bank, not into Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: New Company shares: rightmost applicant enters Court and Debt falls by one while both remain; with no Debt, remaining applicants slide right preserving order. Seek Share says pay bank; it never pays family cash into Company treasuries.

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending order by the number on the backs of their cards. Ordinary hiring of a member of the hirer's own family requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool; Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. When promoting an officeholder, transfer that officeholder's fatigue to the new office card and insert the old card, vacant, in ascending hiring order. If there is no candidate or the hirer is vacant, skip the office: it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.
answers.evidence: Hiring: ascending number; Nepotism requires consent of every other player represented in candidate pool, with Chairman elections and Commander appointments exempt; fatigue transfers on promotion; no candidate or hirer means skip and no actions.

answers.answer: The former Chairman announces a candidate supported by a pure majority of current Company shares (more than half). Any shareholder may campaign, and the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If nobody obtains that support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including themself; Nepotism consent does not apply. The winning Company share is moved into the Chairman slot. It still counts as a share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.
answers.evidence: Chairman election: pure majority of current shares; if no candidate gets support, former Chairman picks any shareholder; the Chairman piece still counts as a share but cannot be traded or invested in firms.

answers.answer: Commit resources and cash first; cash for a Company-office check comes only from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice, subtract penalties, and roll. Use the lowest die: 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office-specific limits permit; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office's actions, returns its officeholder to supply, discards its fatigue, and flips its card into Vacant Offices. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success, such as trading with no ship or deploying with no dice merely to cause possible officer losses.
answers.evidence: Success checks: Company check cash comes from acting office treasury and is paid to bank; lowest die 1–2 success, 3–4 failure/retry if allowed, 5–6 catastrophe; no dead action.

answers.answer: The Chairman may borrow freely for up to three Debt advances, adding £5 to Balance for each. Each further advance requires consent from players controlling a majority of Company shares, with the Chairman counted in that majority. Never advance past the Debt track's end. The Chairman must then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while respecting the borrowing limits. Cash already in office treasuries stays there for those offices to use.
answers.evidence: Chairman: up to three Debt freely, each +£5 Balance; each additional advance requires majority-shareholder consent; never pass Debt track end; allocate all Balance to other offices.

answers.answer: The Manager of Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without the owner's consent, or buy a Company ship for £5, but only if no ships remain on shipyards. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once that office exists. Extra ships serve only until Refresh.
answers.evidence: Manager of Shipping: spend until £2 or less; lease £2, fit £3 without owner consent, buy Company ship £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards; place in any sea zone; extra ships last until Refresh.

answers.answer: The President declares regions for Trade, including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders within available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President's treasury buys one die, and each declared nonhome region subtracts one die. A failed attempt may be retried during that President's opportunity if affordable; a catastrophe removes the President. The President can have at most one successful Trade per turn, and its attempts and retries are uninterrupted by another position. On success, fill one order per ship in that sea zone, as many as possible within the declared regions. The first writer goes to the home port; each next order must be adjacent to one already filled by this Presidency. Use actual writers while available, then filled-order tokens. A Presidency may never fill another Presidency's home region, even if that office is vacant. Increase Balance by each order's printed value, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it that turn under deregulation. The President receives £1 from the bank per order and writer owners receive £1 per writer placed. Use dividers to separate adjacent writers from different Presidencies for Refresh.
answers.evidence: Presidency operations and Trade: declared regions include home and reachable open orders within capacity; £1 per die and -1 per nonhome region; one success per turn; route, writer/token use, protected home regions, revenue and bonuses specified.

answers.answer: A Commander may target a region in their own Presidency (including its home), any associated region, or any region bordering an associated region. They cannot target another Presidency's home or another Presidency's Company-controlled region; a Company region must have unrest or a closed order to provide an effect. Exhaust chosen officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the strength of the target and every other region in its empire, counting the target once (Company-controlled defense strength is zero). Each alliance's strength may be used only once that turn, for Deploy or defense, and cannot be split. Noncatastrophic failure can be retried using remaining resources. After every attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments do not roll officer-loss dice. On catastrophe, return half the Commander's family's trophies rounded up and return the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: target limits and Company-region condition; exhaust pieces for dice and subtract empire strength; alliance use limit; officer loss dice after each attempt; catastrophe destinations.

answers.answer: On a successful Deploy, loot is £4 per target tower plus the faceup loot-token modifier, with a minimum of one plus the number of surviving officers used. Distribute the loot in cycles: £1 to the Commander plus £1 per their surviving used officer; clockwise £1 per other player's surviving used officer; then £1 to the bank per regiment and per alliance piece (not per alliance strength), repeating until the cash is gone. The Commander takes one trophy per target tower. Then impose control by removing the target's tower and dome, removing all matching empire flags if the target was a capital, opening all its orders and clearing unrest. If newly Company-controlled, place its loot/control token region-side above its President and put the Governor overlay in the conquered region, with only the office card placed in Vacant Offices. If the Elephant was in the conquered region and pointed outward, move it fully inside. On catastrophic failure, the Commander returns half their family's trophies rounded up and the Commander member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses, and the Commander has no office card to vacate.
answers.evidence: Commanders and Deploy: success loot formula/distribution/trophies and control procedure; catastrophe returns half trophies and Commander to supply, with officer losses still checked.

answers.answer: Use the Governor's printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without a penalty, then reduces the pool by one. A success pays the Governor £1, plus another £1 if the preceding roll failed, and chooses a benefit: build a Company ship in two successes (first partially built in the region, then a later successful build completes it in the President's associated sea zone); commission a regiment into the associated Army; or tax by adding an unsplit £2 to Balance or the President's treasury. Every Tax after the first this turn adds unrest in the region. Every unsuccessful check adds unrest. The Governor may continue until choosing to stop, running out of dice, or rolling a catastrophe, which follows normal office-removal rules.
answers.evidence: Governors—Administer: current dice pool and decrement; success payments and choices; subsequent Tax unrest; every failure adds unrest; may stop, run out of dice, or suffer catastrophe.

answers.answer: Company expenses are £1 for each existing Debt, each officer or regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone (including China); Commanders are excluded. If Balance cannot cover expenses, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt by one each time until the track end; loans continue even at maximum Debt. Newly added emergency Debt creates no extra expense that turn. After the loans, set Balance to zero. One or two emergency loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then compare remaining Balance with the expectations for the current Standing; if below expectations, lower Standing one. Finally the Chairman may pay affordable dividends, each costing one cash per Company share and paying £1 per share to each owner, including the Chairman. If total dividend cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, advance Standing one space.
answers.evidence: Revenue: expenses include existing Debt/officers/regiments/ships; emergency loans advance Debt and continue at max, with no current extra debt expense; Standing effects, then expectations and dividends.

answers.answer: An Invasion or Rebellion against a Company region triggers secondary Rebellions in every other Company region with unrest. Resolve the primary first, then secondary attacks in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order, with each Commander ordering attacks within their Presidency. For a primary normal Crisis, attack strength is the normal Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in its target. For a primary Foreign Invasion, use its ordinary attack die without adding unrest. Each secondary Rebellion's strength is only the number of unrest cubes in that secondary region, with no event modifier or empire strength. To defend, the associated Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling the attack strength, or as much as possible; local alliances use printed strength and cannot be split. If exhausted strength is insufficient, the region is lost. If sufficient, clear all its unrest and the Commander takes one trophy. If there is no Commander, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces but gains or loses no trophies. A successful primary Invasion against the Company applies empire growth; the summary gives no additional successful-defense procedure beyond clearing unrest and awarding the trophy.
answers.evidence: Attacks on Company: primary and secondary order/strength; Commander exhausts active Army pieces; sufficient defense clears unrest and awards trophy; vacancy substitutes and Company loss procedure.

answers.answer: After voting, support of -1 or less fails: discard the law, resolve a dilemma's If Failed text, return the Opposition Leader token and give the PM dial to the Opposition Leader. The new PM moves the proposed policy one space in either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. Support of zero or higher passes: place the law with passed laws, give the PM a passed-law token, resolve the selected policy first and then the law's immediate effects. Restore all voting cards to their regular orientation after either result. If a law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring.
answers.evidence: Parliament—Resolution: -1 or less fails and changes PM/policy; zero or higher passes and resolves policy before immediate law effects; restore used cards after either outcome.

answers.answer: In the 1758 and Long 1710 scenarios, at the start of a turn before London Season, the PM may call a special Deregulation vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. On passage, reduce Debt by one for every two current Debt, set Standing to S, give the PM a passed-law token, and activate firms. On failure, increase Company-share scoring value by flipping or placing the Court VP token, to a maximum of ±3. This special vote has no policy; failure does not remove the PM or discard the Deregulation law, and the PM may vote against it. The summary says it is a special vote but does not specify further voting-procedure exceptions. The 1813 scenario starts deregulated.
answers.evidence: Deregulation: scenarios and timing; may/must trigger; passage and failure effects; no policy and listed exceptions; 1813 starts deregulated.

answers.answer: During the Firms phase after Family share creation and before Hiring, players may form or invest in firms. To form one, a player not already managing a firm returns one eligible Company share to supply or flips a workshop to its invested side, flips the family board, places a family member as the first firm share, sets the value cube to the leftmost space, and takes £5 from the bank into the firm's London treasury. To invest with the manager's consent, use the same Company-share or workshop contribution to create one firm share and put £5 from the bank into London. A firm can have up to ten shares; additional investments still add £5 but create no share. The Chairman's share cannot be used, Company shares cannot be invested at all when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and shares created that turn cannot be used even if traded away. Invested workshops never return to uninvested status and no longer earn bonuses or Company-failure VP; they remain invested if the firm fails. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.
answers.evidence: Firms phase—Form/Invest: contribution and £5 bank funding, ten-share limit, Chairman and lined-space restrictions, same-turn shares, invested workshop status; firm treasury rules prohibit family cash transfers.

answers.answer: Each manager secretly selects a sea zone and home port plus a London-cash bid; a firm needs at least one ship to select a zone, though its chosen home port may be closed. Hobnob is the alternative: no bid or trade/dividends, but expenses still apply and its prior dividend marker remains. Reveal cash bids simultaneously while strategy cards stay facedown until the associated Presidency begins. At the start of that Presidency's operations, before any actions, matching firms reveal strategy, roll one die per £1 bid, and pay the bid to the bank. At least one die showing 1 or 2 permits trade. Initiative equals ship count minus successful bid dice (1s/2s), and a successful President's Trade sets Company initiative the same way using Presidency ships. After Company Trade succeeds, fill orders from lowest initiative upward; the President decides ties. If the President is vacant or never successfully trades, firms fill after Commanders/Governors have acted, with the Chairman deciding initiative ties. Each firm has one trade attempt per turn and fills up to ships plus one open orders, starting from its home port and tracing a connected route through its own filled orders back there. It may fill any particular order only once, but may refill orders filled by another trader this turn, including the Company; the Company can also refill firm-filled orders. An order already filled this turn pays half its listed revenue, rounded down. Firm Value advances one space for each full £6 added to its India treasury that turn.
answers.evidence: Firm strategies and competing trade: secret choices/bids and reveal timing; dice/check and initiative; order filling timing, capacity/route, repeat fills and half revenue; value growth.

answers.answer: At the start of Revenue, before the Company, firms pay in initiative order (then other firms); ties go by the manager with most windows, then PM clockwise order. Expenses are £1 per charter ship plus the higher of the firm's share count or value, payable from either or both firm treasuries. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends from the India treasury only: each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager, though with the manager's consent a shareholder may forgo payments for any number of shares. Record total actual cash paid out on the dividend marker; an active non-Hobnob firm that pays nothing records zero, while Hobnob retains its old marker. Sweep remaining India money to London. If a firm cannot pay expenses, it dissolves unless rescued through emergency investments or merger with one other firm (which must first pay its own expenses if due and cover the unpaid amount). On dissolution, firm shares go to Debtor's Prison and each costs its owner 1 VP, ships return to shipyards, the charter returns to the family side, and workshops remain invested.
answers.evidence: Firm expenses/rescue/dividends: expense formula and eligible treasuries; India-only dividends and marker; failure rescue/dissolution destinations and workshop status.
